One user created an account only to be told Runway doesn't work unless you're using Chrome.

A user who tried it said that with very little work they produced a near-seamless mask that adapted to dynamic, changing poses. The main drawback was speed: most edits needed more than 20 seconds of loading/buffering, even on a 1Gbps connection. They called the lag a potential major productivity killer and suspected a native app would be faster.

Concern about the cloud model: uploading video assets to their servers seems extremely impractical for 4K or 8K footage. Even with gigabit upload, a clip could take several times its playback duration to transfer.

A professional video editor/VFX artist said this won't get used by professionals. The ML tech is better than what's built into After Effects, but fixing their existing software's mistakes takes less time than learning narrower new software. They suggested shipping it as a plugin for Fusion, Nuke or Hitfilm instead.
Cost comparison: the automated masking looks impressive, but DaVinci Resolve does the same for a one-off £250 lifetime license. At $35/month, Resolve works out cheaper in under 10 months.

Many of these ML features already exist in DaVinci Resolve, which is free and lightning fast. The commenter saw value for people who don't want to learn professional software, but wanted a client-side version that runs models on their own gaming GPUs.

A skeptic said it looks like a GUI over public TensorFlow Hub models: AI masking, depth estimation, flow estimation, and 'flicker artifacts just like the public AI models.' They noted similar tools (unscreen, Comixify) and AI rotoscoping in DaVinci Resolve 17.

The foreground/background separations look magic but cherry-picked: a fixed-camera skater against a contrasting background and a figure on a misty background are easy targets. The depth maps look more promising, good enough for a decent fog pass. The commenter is unsure about cloud-based use, since bandwidth issues are making their online video students drop out.

A former film pro said nothing here is 'impossible,' just previously labor-intensive, but if the demos are representative it's 'slick as hell.' The browser/cloud model is a big barrier for remote productions with huge data volumes, and raises security, downtime and project-export concerns. They called it an instant win for short-form work like music videos, commercials and demo reels.
Several users were enthusiastic: 'Wow I'm extremely impressed. This is clearly the future of video editing — and deep fakes,' and 'THIS. IS. INCREDIBLE.'
A ScreenFlow user said Runway looks much more powerful and innovative than their current tool and plans to try it.

A filmmaker said Runway's site, along with a Two Minute Papers video, convinced them to teach themselves ML. They see it as an alternative to green screen, which they called big, bulky, expensive and a pain to set up and light.
